newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: SOCCER-COLOMBIA COMES UP SMELLING COCAINE AND CHEESE IN SOCCER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOMBIA COMES UP SMELLING COCAINE AND CHEESE IN SOCCER.

text.p: The goalscorer in Colombia's 1-0 win over Ecuador in a World Cup qualifying match Sunday dedicated the victory to the country's jailed cocaine kingpins while President Ernesto Samper said the triumph had the "smell of French cheese and Colombian coffee".

"I'd like to dedicate the goal to all those who for some reason or another are deprived of their freedom. I'd like to dedicate it to Miguel and Gilberto Rodriguez (Orejuela)," striker Anthony De Avila told reporters after his 86th minute goal.
The Rodriguez Orejuela brothers headed the Cali drug cartel, estimated to have been responsible for 80 percent of the world cocaine supply, before their capture in mid-1995.
De Avila currently plays for the New York-based Metro Stars team but previously played in Colombia for the Cali-based America team, of which the Rodriguezes were reputed to be the main shareholders.
The triumph, which follows a recent spell of lackluster performances, brings Colombia a step closer to earning a place in soccer's World Cup finals in France next year.
Minutes after the end of the match, as he inaugurated a new session of Congress in Bogota, Samper told legislators: "The victory has the flavor of French cheese and the smell of Colombian coffee."
Samper, who allegedly financed his 1994 election campaign with $6 million from the Cali cartel, was apparently unaware of De Avila's controversial comments.
